fields.reasoning: Read the change set's intent, ship-main-tree-check, shipCheckMainTree and shipRerunFailed in internal/api/ship.go, the wait-main/main-green steps in ship-change.toml, .github/workflows/ci.yml and the ci install template in internal/api/ci.go. (1) The parent #256 served milestone-25 and this is a fix that lets daemon-built change sets ship, which is exactly that milestone. (2) workflow_dispatch takes only a branch or tag, so --ref <sha> fails; dispatching on main alone would test main's tip, which may already hold later merges and so would not prove the merge commit green. A sha input plus checkout ref pins the tested commit, and a run-name carrying the sha gives ship a reliable way to find the run it dispatched without racing other dispatches. (3) ship-change is generic across repos, so hard-coding ci.yml is wrong; the workflows that matter are the ones that gate PRs, and only ones declaring workflow_dispatch can be dispatched. Stopping loudly when none exist keeps the no-untested-main guarantee instead of silently passing. (4) Matching the PR checks' existing rerun-once policy absorbs flaky runners consistently; beyond that a red main needs a human, as the old main-green did on push CI failure (it had no on.fail), and an automatic revert would be a new, unasked-for behaviour.
fields.statement: (1) Change set 01M6MA6P serves milestone-25 (empty the backlog), like its parent #256: it unblocks the daemon's own shipping. (2) The dispatched run tests the merge commit itself, pinned by input, not main's tip: ship runs `gh workflow run <file> --ref main -f sha=<merge commit>`; the workflow's workflow_dispatch trigger declares a required `sha` input, checks out `ref: ${{ inputs.sha || github.sha }}`, and sets `run-name` to include the sha, so ship finds its run by the sha in the run's display title (event workflow_dispatch) and waits on it, never on whatever main has advanced to. (3) Ship dispatches every workflow file under .github/workflows that declares both a pull_request and a workflow_dispatch trigger (the workflows that gate PRs and can be dispatched); in this repo that is ci.yml, and the `rhiza ci install` template gains the same workflow_dispatch trigger with the sha input. When the trees differ and no such workflow exists, the main step stops with a stop: line naming the merge commit and saying no dispatchable workflow was found. Trees equal: nothing is dispatched, as now. (4) A dispatched run that fails gets the same one rerun of its failed jobs that PR checks get (shipRerunFailed, once per merge commit); if it still fails, main-green fails with a stop: line naming the merge commit and the failed checks, and the run stops for a person: no revert, no automatic fix, no close-out.
